title: Chikok chico (NSIC Sd 02): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Chikok chico: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Chikok chico is a chico variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Chikok is a registered chico variety, also sold or known as NSIC Sd 02. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2005 as NSIC 2005 Sd 02. Prevada Fresco bred it. Its record notes a yield of 52.66 kg.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Sd 02, this is the same chico. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [chico variety finder](/crop-varieties/chico), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Chikok was about 15 years old and about 15 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 52.66 kg. It bears fruit in December March. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit chico fields most often: [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Chikok weighs about 154.63 grams, and its shape is oblong. The flesh is brown and smooth and firm. Its sweetness measured 19.49 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 78.8 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as December March, bearing regular and sometimes 2 times a year.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** About 53 kg per tree a year.
**Fruit:** Oblong, about 155 g, brown skin, smooth, firm, juicy brown flesh, about 19.5 Brix, about 79 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a Guimaras chico with larger fruit (about 155 g) that sometimes bears twice a year. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Chikok chico

Pick a selection with big, sweet fruit and few seeds, and plant marcotted or grafted trees. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Sd 02 the same as Chikok?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Sd 02 is another name for Chikok, registered as NSIC 2005 Sd 02. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 52.66 kg. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Chikok?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
